subject: Tenant affinity & routing acceptance for EU/APAC private deployment
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@acmefin.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liu Wei <liu.wei@cyberops.cn>; Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@telco-apac.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Tenant affinity and routing — acceptance criteria and evidence request

Alex,

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough. We're progressing on our compliance checklist and have two concrete asks before our security board will sign off for the private deployment in EU and the warm-standby in APAC:

1) A clear tenant affinity guarantee for EU traffic (how sessions are pinned to EU clusters and under what failure modes traffic will be evacuated to APAC).
2) Network-level evidence (sample BGP policy / peering matrix and the topology diagram you walked through) plus a short runbook showing the manual failover steps and rollback.

I've attached our current topology sketch — please point us to the exact artifacts Redwood will provide (diagram + config snippets) and the expected SLA impact. We need these by next Tuesday (30 Jun) for the board packet.

Regards,
Samir Desai
Head of Infrastructure, AcmeFin
attachments: acmefin-eu-apac-topology.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@acmefin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 16:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Tenant affinity and routing — acceptance criteria and evidence request

Samir —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers and plan:

- Tenant affinity guarantee: Redwood Private will pin tenant sessions to the EU private cluster by default using destination-based routing + a consistent hash at the edge proxy. The policy is: keep active sessions/kv-caches in EU unless EU loses control-plane peering for >30s; after 30s, traffic will be rerouted to the APAC warm-standby cluster with an explicit emergency header. We will document the exact cookie/hash algorithm and the affinity TTL.

- Evidence & artifacts: we'll provide the network topology PDF (redwood-acmefin-topology.pdf), a sample BGP policy export (text), and a two-page manual runbook for the evacuation/rollback. I'll start a combined packet and aim to get the draft to you by EOD Monday.

Next steps (proposed):
- Monica will coordinate the network config snippets and the BGP example.
- Jonas will own the runbook and acceptance test steps (HTTP-level checks + token pinning validation).

Alex Martinez
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: draft: topology & BGP examples

Alex / Jonas — attaching the two files: 1) redwood-acmefin-topology.pdf (diagram showing EU primary, APAC warm-standby with explicit cross-region peering), 2) tenant-affinity-matrix.xlsx (affinity TTLs, cookie/hash details, and failover thresholds).

Highlights:
- Affinity enforcement lives at the edge proxy and is consistent across the private cluster via KV sync. We recommend TTL 10m for active sessions, with a 30s session health check window to detect EU control-plane evacuation.
- Failover behavior: on EU control-plane loss, we mark the tenant as "evacuating" and advertise a route to APAC using a low-preference community. The BGP snippet is sanitized but matches operational config.
- Acceptance test: we include curl + header checks to verify the emergency header and the cookie that indicates affinity. Jonas, please confirm the test steps are actionable.

attachments: redwood-acmefin-topology.pdf, tenant-affinity-matrix.xlsx

Monica Patel
Network Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@acmefin.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:47:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Tenant affinity and routing — acceptance criteria and evidence request

Samir —

I've reviewed the artifacts and attached the final acceptance checklist to this thread (pasted below for convenience). We validated the curl-based tests against our staging warm-standby:

Acceptance checklist (summary):
- Topology diagram with peering map: attached (redwood-acmefin-topology.pdf)
- BGP policy example: included inline and sanitized
- Affinity TTL and hashing algo: documented in matrix (tenant-affinity-matrix.xlsx)
- Manual failover runbook: embedded procedures + rollback steps (2 pages)
- Test steps: provided curl checks and CDN cache invalidation procedure

Expected SLA impact on failover: during evacuation, median tail p50 -> p95 latency may increase by ~90-120ms due to cross-region hop; token validation and KV warming add a small bootstrap window (~45s). No data persistence loss expected — KV caches are read-through and durable.

If this looks good, I will upload the artifacts to the shared Drive link and mark the board packet as ready.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-acmefin-topology.pdf, tenant-affinity-matrix.xlsx, runbook-evacuation.pdf
